concepts.executive_explanation: Whether the site understands normal shopper typing variations such as plurals, missing apostrophes, shorthand wording, and category variants.
concepts.why_it_matters: Good normalization keeps motivated shoppers from needing exact menu labels or catalog-perfect wording.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether the site handles multi-word fashion phrases as customer intent rather than isolated words.
concepts.why_it_matters: Boutique shoppers often search in phrases such as little black dress, square neck top, or two piece set.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether customer wording maps to retailer language: going out top, date night dress, brunch outfit, vacation dress, and similar terms.
concepts.why_it_matters: Customer-language coverage makes product finding feel natural and reduces browsing effort.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether product type, color, occasion, team, style, and accessory fields appear to influence what rises first.
concepts.why_it_matters: Strong first results create confidence because shoppers quickly see that the store understands their intent.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether broader needs such as wedding guest outfit, graduation dress, teacher outfit, or vacation outfit expand into useful products.
concepts.why_it_matters: Expansion helps shoppers who know the occasion but not the exact item name.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether searchable fields include useful fashion attributes such as fabric, cut, neckline, sleeve, stretch, and fit.
concepts.why_it_matters: Attribute coverage lets shoppers search by the details that make an item feel right.

concepts.executive_explanation: Whether Spanish or mixed Spanish-English searches can guide shoppers to English-language boutique products.
concepts.why_it_matters: Bilingual discovery is a market-access issue: shoppers should not need English catalog-perfect language to find products.
